_doc: Meeting script templates for crewmates. Keys are situations detected by the engine. Placeholders: {P} target player, {R} room, {T} time (m:ss), {W} witness, {V} victim, {TASK} task name, {N} number. Each entry: question templates (ask), statement templates (say), what to watch for. Lines are plain chat language (<= 70 chars, no commas chains) because they get copied into the game chat as is.
principles: Give your own location + companion FIRST. It pre-empts accusations and models the behaviour you want.
Lead with hard clears. A confirmed-crew list is the most valuable thing you can say.
Ask questions whose answers can be checked against what someone else saw.
Make people commit to a story early; contradictions only exist once stories are on record.
Vote skip when nobody has evidence. A wrong eject is worth more than a kill to the impostors.
Watch who agrees without adding info. Bandwagons hide impostors.
Count. Alive crew vs impostors decides whether a skip is safe.

say: I was in {R} with {W} all round.
{P} is clear, I saw them do {TASK} in {R}.
ask: Where was everyone when the body was found?
watch: Anyone who answers with a question instead of a location.

ask: {P} why were you in {R} and who did you see on the way?
{P} what task do you have in {R}?
say: {P} reported alone in {R}. Nobody saw them go in.
watch: If {P} names a task that isn't in {R} on this map.
If {P} names a companion who then denies it.

ask: {R} is a dead end. Who went in or came out? I saw {P} leave around {T}.
say: Body in {R}, one way in. Last one through that door explains.
watch: Vent networks touching {R}: anyone who 'appeared' nearby without passing the door.

ask: {P} you were with {V} in {R} around {T}. Where did you split?
say: Last one I saw with {V} was {P} in {R} around {T}.
watch: Whether {P} offers the split location unprompted or deflects.

ask: {P} you said {TASK} in {R}. Everyone has that task. Who else did it?
say: I dont have {TASK}. Common tasks are the same for everyone.
watch: Anyone who suddenly 'also has it' with no location.
This is near-proof if the lobby's common tasks are known.

say: {TASK} is not in {R}. {P} which panel did you use?
watch: Specificity. Crew can name the panel; impostors go vague.

say: Visuals are on. Nobody saw {P} do {TASK}.
watch: If {P} downgrades to a non-visual task after being asked.

ask: When lights went off who went to fix them? {P} came late from {R}.
say: Kill was during lights. Whoever was lost in the dark is the question.
watch: Anyone who claims they were 'on the way' but arrived from the wrong direction.

ask: {P} reactor was called and you were at neither panel. Where were you?
say: {W} and I fixed {TASK} together so {W} is clear.
watch: Who benefits from a split: the impostor usually ends up on the smaller side.

say: {P} said {R} at {T} but {W} saw {P} in {R2}. One of those is wrong.
That is not what {P} said last meeting.
ask: {P} {W} says you were in {R2} not {R}. Which is it?
watch: Whether {P} attacks {W}'s credibility instead of answering.

ask: {P} what did you actually see? Sus is not a location.
say: {P} is pushing {P2} with no sighting. Where were you {P}?
watch: Impostors often accuse first to look proactive.

say: Only hard clears count now. {W} is confirmed crew.
ask: {P} and {P2} where were you for the last kill? Room and time.
watch: The impostor will try to make it a vibe vote. Keep it to kill windows.

say: Nobody has anything. Skip and move in pairs.
ask: Everyone say your room and who you were with.
watch: Who resists committing to a location.

say: {P} hard defended {P2} who was impostor. Pair tell.
ask: {P} why were you so sure {P2} was clear?
watch: Any two players who never vote each other across meetings.

say: Kill in the stack. {P} {P2} {P3} were all there. Who was closest to {V}?
ask: {P} {P2} {P3} who was next to the body before the report?
watch: The one who claims they 'didn't notice' the kill.
